en.title: Maximum Node Sum of a Downward Path from Any Start
en.description:
The tree is rooted at 0. Choose a non-empty path that only goes downward, edge by edge from parent to child, starting at any node, and find the maximum node sum. The path cannot pass through a node to join two subtrees. The stable-segment example that Fastprep pasted by mistake does not belong to this problem.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site; missing numeric bounds and recoveries of source typos are all stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains n parent entries, and the third line contains n value entries. Complete OCR range: 1≤n≤100000, parent[0]=−1, the others are in 0..n−1 and form a valid tree; values are in −1000..1000, and a parent index is not guaranteed to be smaller than its child's index.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 20; 20; -2. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Traverse iteratively to get an order in which parents come before children, then process it in reverse to compute each node's best downward sum: its own value plus the largest positive child path; the answer is the maximum over all nodes.
